endorsements.quote: System monitoring and evaluation at regular intervals can help ensure the prevention of potential harm creation or perpetuation.

Although it is not necessary to recreate the entire ethical evaluation pipeline, it is considered best practice to reapply the original assessment metrics established during initial development (outlined in Part 2 [Assessment]).
A comprehensive regulatory review should be conducted before any AI development begins.
Acceptance criteria establish the conditions a system must meet before release.
This may involve evaluating performance across subgroups, measuring disparities in false positives or negatives, or assessing equal access to beneficial outcomes.

By embedding these statistical guardrails directly into the acceptance criteria, SAFE-AI ensures that monitoring processes in Part 4 are both preplanned and directly linked to the responsibility metrics established during development.
This ensures that even behind-the-scenes model improvements are held to the same standards of validation, risk assessment, and accountability.
Risk analysis should be conducted collaboratively, including consultation with relevant stakeholders like product teams, data scientists, and legal experts.

After completing the above, the decision-making stakeholders should come together as part of an existing review or showcase discussion to review the report, analyze the results, and come to a consensus on whether or not the work is "good enough" to proceed to deployment.
AI developers and AI deployers should maintain a governance framework that is backed by sufficient executive oversight.

unlisted_practices: Create custom ethical cards from project objectives and risks and write them into the Agile backlog as user stories or research spikes with acceptance criteria and clear owners.
Co-develop acceptance criteria with key stakeholders, including clinicians, patients, domain experts, and end users.
Use scenario-based probability analogy mapping to translate model errors, uncertainty, and risk into plain-language narratives for nontechnical stakeholders.

Re-enter the ethical evaluation process whenever a change could materially affect model behavior, fairness, or transparency, such as retraining, hyperparameter tuning, feature changes, or new external datasets.
Include organizational leadership with authority to make go or no-go decisions, and make company leadership accountable for those decisions on high-risk systems.

screen.reason: The paper describes the co-design of a governance/development framework (SAFE-AI) embedding ethical safeguards into agile workflows for medical AI SMEs. No operational deployment or empirical testing of an AI model's performance was conducted.
